source: Census Bureau Oct. 2026 data via Reuters; Realtor.com

headline: Building permits
hit a *2020 low*
slides.fig_caption: Total building permits in October (annual rate), the fewest since May 2020
slides.sub: Starts jumped in October, but permits, the early signal for future building, fell 7.4% in a month.

slides.title: October housing starts, *change vs. September*
slides.note: Total starts reached 1.309M, well above the 1.245M economists expected. *Apartments (5+ units) did most of the lifting.*

slides.label: single-family permits, *down 8.7%* from September
slides.body: That's the fewest since January 2023, and permits fell in all four regions. In the Midwest, single-family starts also slipped 0.8%, the only region to decline.

slides.title: Fewer new homes *on deck*
slides.body: Permits come before shovels, so today's pullback means less new-build competition for resale listings down the road. With the 30-year rate at 7.18%, builders are still clearing unsold homes, so expect incentives to stay in play.
